patient.key: Irritability, eczema, musty-smelling urine — the PKU triad in a newborn

sequence.decision: Recognize the metabolic newborn — mousy/musty odor is pathognomonic for PKU. Don't chase infection.
Classic PKU: eczema from phenylalanine accumulation in skin, musty odor from phenylacetic acid in sweat/urine.

sequence.what: LP, CSF cultures, galactokinase, cryptococcal antigen, fungal culture, viral culture, cytology — a complete meningitis workup
sequence.decision: Wrong direction. This is a metabolic disease, not an infection. The only test needed: serum phenylalanine.

sequence.what: Phenylalanine, serum would confirm PKU. Treatment: low protein diet + nutrition consult.
sequence.decision: One blood test diagnoses. One dietary change treats. The case is that simple — once you recognize it.

missed.why: The diagnostic test. PAH deficiency blocks phenylalanine → tyrosine conversion. Serum phenylalanine >20 mg/dL (this patient: 21.47 mg/dL) is diagnostic. Normal is <2 mg/dL. This one $10 test replaces your entire meningitis workup — and scores the 45% diagnostic weight.

The treatment. PKU is managed by restricting dietary phenylalanine. Special low-phenylalanine formula + breast milk in measured amounts. This is for life. Without it: intellectual disability, seizures, white matter lesions. Treatment scored 0% because you ordered zero therapeutic interventions.

correctMoves: Physical exam focused on skin (eczema) and genitalia (odd smell)
Recognized the patient was ill enough to work up
No inappropriate invasive orders (LP attempt in a 3-week-old is not penalized if meningitis is suspected)

trapExplanation.name: PKU is a trap name
trapExplanation.detail: Phenylketonuria suggests urine testing, but PKU is diagnosed via serum phenylalanine. Standard UA ketones screen for acetoacetic acid and beta-hydroxybutyrate — the ketones in PKU (phenylacetic acid) are not detected by routine UA. The name is historical, not diagnostic.

mechanismsForImage.title: PAH Enzyme Block — Where the Train Derails
mechanismsForImage.concept: Phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH) is broken. Phenylalanine cannot become tyrosine. The backup pathway produces phenylacetic acid — the musty odor. Brain LAT1 transporters get saturated, starving neurons of tyrosine and tryptophan. Myelination fails. IQ drops irreversibly.

mechanismsForImage.title: Metabolic Newborn Differential — The Four Smells
mechanismsForImage.concept: PKU (musty/mousy), MSUD (maple syrup/burnt sugar), Galactosemia (no smell — silent), Isovaleric Acidemia (sweaty feet). The UA dipstick cannot distinguish them. The smell + timeline can. MSUD crashes in 4-7 days. PKU is insidious over weeks.

mechanismsForImage.title: The Trap — Why PKU Is Diagnosed in Blood, Not Urine
mechanismsForImage.concept: The name ends in -uria, suggesting urine testing. But standard UA ketones test for acetoacetate (nitroprusside reaction). PKU's ketone (phenylacetic acid) does NOT react. Serum phenylalanine is the diagnostic test. One lavender-top tube.
